title: Find the largest file in a folder in the Files app

setup.why: A fresh folder for this run in Download with four text files of different sizes; the largest is {{f.kb}} kB, the others 3 to 21 kB, and none sorts first by name for being largest.

argv: d=/sdcard/Download/computer-bench-{{nonce}}; rm -rf $d && mkdir -p $d && head -c {{f.kb}}000 /dev/zero > $d/{{f.big}}-{{nonce}}.txt && head -c 21000 /dev/zero > $d/{{f.a}}-{{nonce}}.txt && head -c 3000 /dev/zero > $d/{{f.b}}-{{nonce}}.txt && head -c 12000 /dev/zero > $d/{{f.c}}-{{nonce}}.txt

setup.why: Open the system file manager (DocumentsUI) on the run's folder.

instruction: Using the Files app, which file in Download/computer-bench-{{nonce}} is the largest? Give its file name in your final answer. Don't change anything.

checks.why: The final answer names {{f.big}}, the largest file, before any of the other three (an answer may go on to list the rest). An agent that answers nothing fails, and so does one that names a smaller file first.
The folder still holds the four files: the agent read it and changed nothing.

teardown.why: Delete the run's folder and everything in it.

oracle.why: Wait for the folder's listing: on a fresh phone it shows a moment after am start -W returns.
The list view shows each file's size. The answer itself is the agent's to give; verify leaves answer checks out of the oracle's run.
